title: Case study: distributed key-value store

kcs.statement: A Dynamo-style key-value store places each key on a hash ring and replicates it to the next N distinct nodes clockwise. Virtual nodes spread load evenly when nodes join or leave.
With N replicas, choosing R + W > N makes every read overlap the latest write. Choosing R = W = 1 maximises availability and speed but allows stale reads.

In a leaderless store, concurrent writes to one key can conflict. They are resolved by last-write-wins timestamps or by returning sibling versions, and replicas converge through read repair and background anti-entropy.

problem_ideas: With N = 3, list the (R, W) pairs that give strong reads and say which one favours write latency.
Draw where key 'user:42' and its two replicas land on a ring of 4 nodes with 3 virtual nodes each.
A node is down for 10 minutes during writes. Explain how the data catches up afterwards.
Two clients write the same cart key concurrently. Compare last-write-wins with keeping both versions.
Estimate the node count for 50 TB of data at replication factor 3 and 2 TB usable per node.
Say whether this store is CP or AP under a network partition with R = W = 1.
